title: New Forms of Money and the U.S. Monetary Aggregates
date_evidence: Date: September 04, 2026; Authors: Kristen Payne and Mary-Frances Styczynski
key_claim: The Federal Reserve's own FEDS Note states payment stablecoins are prohibited from paying interest directly to holders, but concedes indirect compensation may still be possible.
frame_summary: The Federal Reserve is arguing that stablecoins strain the existing framework for measuring money itself, not just bank funding, and flags the direct/indirect interest distinction as an open definitional problem for its own accounting, not a settled compliance matter.
verbatim_quote: Also, payment stablecoins are prohibited from paying interest directly to stablecoin holders, though indirect compensation may be possible.

publisher: The White House (Council of Economic Advisers)
title: Effects of Stablecoin Yield Prohibition on Bank Lending
key_claim: The CEA's model finds that eliminating stablecoin yield would raise bank lending by only $2.1 billion (0.02% of bank loans), at a net welfare cost of $0.8 billion, a cost-benefit ratio of 6.6 to 1 against the ban.
frame_summary: The White House is arguing that the deposit-flight case for banning stablecoin yield is quantitatively weak and that the yield prohibition itself is the policy imposing an unjustified welfare cost, reframing the debate from bank safety to consumer benefit forgone.
verbatim_quote: At baseline calibration of CEA's model, eliminating stablecoin yield increases bank lending by $2.1 billion and has a net welfare cost of $800 million.
verbatim_list: That translates into an increase in lending of 0.02% and a cost-benefit ratio of 6.6.

title: Beyond stablecoins: The emerging architecture of on-chain money
date_evidence: Published Date: May 21, 2026; Authors: Matt Higginson, Uzayr Jeenah
key_claim: McKinsey estimates that for every $1,000 converted from a bank deposit into a third-party stablecoin such as USDC, only about 15% returns to the banking system as wholesale reserves, with the rest becoming Treasury securities outside the lending system; the firm treats the GENIUS Act's yield restriction as a factor slowing that migration.
frame_summary: McKinsey is arguing that on-chain money is consolidating into a single monetary stack in which stablecoins, tokenised deposits and central bank money compete on functional terms, and that regulatory yield restrictions on stablecoins are one of the few structural features currently protecting bank balance sheets from faster deposit migration.
verbatim_quote: for every $1,000 converted into a third-party stablecoin, only 15 percent returns to the banking system as wholesale reserves

title: OCC races to finalize GENIUS Act stablecoin rules by November
date_evidence: By Sarah Wynn, Edited by Jason Shubnell, Regulation, August 19, 2026, 1:03PM EDT
key_claim: Comptroller Jonathan Gould committed to a final GENIUS Act stablecoin rule by November 2026, after the OCC and other agencies missed a July deadline, so that stablecoin issuer charter applications can begin processing in the new year.
frame_summary: The Block is arguing that the OCC's rulemaking timeline, not the pace of legislation, is now the operative constraint on when the stablecoin regulatory perimeter (including issuer charters) actually takes effect.
verbatim_quote: So we are very intent on moving quickly and getting a final rule out by November so that we will be able to start processing applications within the new year.
verbatim_list: Agencies like the OCC, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, and others were directed to finalize rules by July, but missed that initial deadline.

title: The OCC's November Deadline Is the Only Federal Stablecoin Game Left in Town
key_claim: With the CLARITY Act dead, the OCC's federal charter for payment stablecoin issuers, with a $10 billion market-cap threshold for transition to federal oversight, is now the only live federal stablecoin framework; 40 charter applications have been filed in 18 months.
frame_summary: Forkast is arguing that legislative failure has made OCC administrative rulemaking, rather than Congress, the de facto venue where the federal stablecoin regulatory perimeter gets decided this cycle.
verbatim_quote: In the 18 months since the OCC began accepting digital-asset-related charter applications, 40 applications have been received.
verbatim_list: We will have a final rule out by November.
The critical threshold is $10 billion: issuers exceeding this market cap are expected to transition to federal oversight.

title: Bad information about stablecoin rewards is running rampant
date_evidence: By Faryar Shirzad, Published September 14, 2026, 7:35 a.m. EDT
key_claim: Coinbase's chief policy officer argues the often-cited $6.6 trillion deposit-flight figure was never a forecast, and that community bank deposits grew 26% ($491 billion) over the seven years to June 2026 alongside stablecoin reward growth, disputing the bank industry's deposit-flight case.
frame_summary: The author, Coinbase's chief policy officer, is arguing that the banking industry's opposition to stablecoin rewards rests on debunked or misleading statistics and amounts to protectionism against a competitive, healthily-coexisting product rather than a genuine financial-stability concern.
verbatim_quote: The $6.6 trillion was not a forecast of deposit flight; it was at the time the entire collective balance held in U.S. transaction accounts.
verbatim_list: Community bank deposits have grown 26% ($491 billion) over the seven-year period ending June 2026.
notes: Author is Coinbase's Chief Policy Officer; published as opinion in a Tier 3 trade venue. Treated directionally as the industry's own counter-case, not as independent verification of the deposit-growth figures.

title: Crypto's biggest Senate push falls flat as the Clarity Act fails to clear a crucial procedural vote
date_evidence: By Jesse Hamilton, Edited by Nikhilesh De, Published Sep 15, 2026, 2:50 p.m. EDT
key_claim: The CLARITY Act failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on 15 September 2026, well short of the 60 votes needed to advance, killing the compromise stablecoin-yield language for this Congress.
frame_summary: CoinDesk is arguing that the CLARITY Act's collapse was a structural defeat for comprehensive market-structure legislation, not a minor procedural delay, leaving agency rulemaking as the only near-term venue for resolving open questions like stablecoin yield.
verbatim_quote: a 49-50 vote meant to start the bill toward passage fell far short in rounding up the 60 supporters required to advance

title: What Is a Stablecoin Reward, and Why Did the CLARITY Act's Failure Keep It Alive?
date_evidence: By Sam Daodu, Published September 18, 2026, 7:10pm ET
key_claim: Circle reported average USDC circulation of $76.5 billion in Q2 2026, generating $668 million in reserve income which it shares with Coinbase, which in turn earned $292 million from stablecoins (about a quarter of its revenue); the CLARITY Act's compromise language on rewards died with the bill, leaving the reward mechanism intact by default.
frame_summary: The author is arguing that stablecoin rewards persist not because regulators approved them but because Congress failed to act, so a multi-hundred-million-dollar quarterly payment channel keeps running on the strength of a legislative vacuum rather than a deliberate policy choice.
verbatim_quote: In Q2 2026, Circle reported an average USDC circulation of $76.5 billion, yielding $668 million in reserve income, a 5% year-over-year increase.
verbatim_list: Circle collects that as reserve income and shares it with Coinbase, which distributes a portion to users as rewards.
Coinbase earned $292 million from stablecoins, about a quarter of its total revenue.
